impraegno (inpr- ), ātum, 1, v. a. in-praegno,
I.to impregnate, make pregnant (late Lat.; perh. only in part. perf.): illa ab eo impregnata vidit in somnis per fauces introisse solem, etc., Myth. Vat. ap. Mai. Auct. Class. t. 3, p. 117.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
